title: Sustainable Altruism: Simulating the Future of Prosociality and Peacebuilding—A Conceptual Review
abstract: In this article, we argue for the potential value of participatory multi-agent artificial intelligence (MAAI) modeling for addressing the pragmatic challenge of promoting a sustainable altruism among individuals and groups that will enable us to find pathways of collective action that lead toward more peaceful coexistence. Along the way, we note that this approach to modeling also addresses the scientific challenge within computer science and social simulation of creating more psychologically realistic artificial agents whose interactions occur in more realistic social networks. We identify some of the evolved cognitive and coalitional biases that make it so difficult to achieve an equilibrium of sustainable altruism in contemporary human societies, describe some of the innovative ways in which recent advances in MAAI approaches to psychological and cultural modeling open up new opportunities for simulating solutions to these challenges, and address some of the ethical issues associated with using modeling and simulating methods to help us proactively navigate the Anthropocene.

title: Pain in the media: A content analysis of pain-related events in 'Made for Kids' YouTube videos.
abstract: During childhood, children are presented with ample opportunities to learn about pain, including through their own experiences and interactions with others. Another possible source of influence is the media they consume. Portrayals of pain in children's television, movies and picture books have previously been examined; however, less is known about other mediums, like YouTube, that reach millions of children. This study aimed to investigate how pain-related events are portrayed in popular children's YouTube videos. Videos from 15 popular 'Made for Kids' YouTube channels (30 videos/channel) were screened for pain-related events. Channels were selected based on popularity (highest subscribers and views). Videos that included pain-related events were analysed using codes adapted from previous studies of pain in children's media. Pain-related events were commonly represented and present in 174 videos, with impact portrayals (i.e., where pain and or injury would be expected in real life, but no evidence of either was present) being the most frequent, followed by minor pain/injury. Boy characters experienced pain-related events more frequently than girl characters, but girls demonstrated more prosocial behaviours in response to sufferers than boys. Characters/presenters with racialized identities were underrepresented in pain-related events, yet racial stereotypes of violence were present. Findings of this study align with previous work investigating portrayals of pain in children's popular television, movies and picture books; demonstrating that sociocultural messaging about pain is consistent across different types of children's media. Future research should consider children's perspectives on pain-related events in popular children's media. PERSPECTIVE: This article describes the frequency and characteristics of pain-related events in popular 'Made for Kids' YouTube videos. Understanding the characteristics of this content is an essential step in understanding how pain may be socialised to children in their everyday media engagement.

title: KORTİZOLÜN NÖROFİNANSAL KODLARI
abstract: İnsanların biyolojik ve psikolojik açıdan strese yanıt olarak ürettiği kortizolün etkileri, bir stres hormonu şeklinde anılmasından öte bir olgudur.Kortizole ilişkin özellikler, stres altındaki bireylerin finansal davranışlarını anlamada ve incelemede bilimsel bir araç olarak kullanılmasını mümkün kılar.Kortizolün ölçülebilir olması ve laboratuvar ortamında deneysel olarak manipüle edilebilmesi nörofinans alanında kayda değer bir imkân yaratmaktadır.Ayrıca kortizol düzeylerindeki varyasyonların karar verme mekanizmaları üzerindeki etkileri gerçekçi ve kapsamlı modeller geliştirilmesine olanak tanır.Böylece stresin finansal davranışlar üzerindeki biyolojik temelleri daha iyi anlaşılabilir ve piyasa dinamiklerine ilişkin öngörüler güçlendirilir.Bu çalışmada da kortizolün, bireylerin ekonomik ve finansal karar verme süreçlerinde, özellikle risk ve belirsizlik durumlarında nasıl rol oynadığı; ödül ve ceza öğrenme merkezli süreçlerin ya da yaklaşımın bilişsel işlevler, motivasyon ve prososyal davranışlar üzerindeki etkileri ele alınmaktadır.Nitekim beynin bu süreçlerde kritik bir biyokimyasal modülatör olduğu, kararların hızını, kalitesini ve risk algısını etkileyerek ekonomik ajanın davranışlarında dikkate değer değişikliklere yol açtığı vurgulanmaktadır.

title: Empathy, Sympathy, and Compassion: Navigating the Landscape of Emotional Resonance
abstract: Positive social interactions are crucial for our well-being. According to Fredrickson, the key to these interactions is positivity resonance, a form of positive emotional resonance that requires shared positive emotions, mutual care, and psychophysical synchrony. To achieve this, we must recognise emotions and have a fundamental ability to perceive others. Arnold’s research delves deeper into emotional reverberation, suggesting that emotional contagion arises merely from shared emotions. Empathy, sympathy, and compassion, instead, are all forms of emotional resonance that require a dynamic understanding of others’ emotions. As humans, we can interpret both our own and others’ emotional experiences, although there is some confusion between empathy and sympathy. While the two concepts may seem similar, psychologists and phenomenologists aim to clarify their essential differences. Sympathy is a positive emotion that highlights our affective consciousness and capacity for social cognition. This article argues that positive emotional resonance (Fredrickson’s notion of love) is sympathy’s psychophysiological scaffolding or counterpart. It also argues the ethical dimension of sympathy and compassion since we can foster them through moral decisions and habituation. Ultimately, it highlights the impact of sharing positive emotions on interpersonal interactions.

title: Safeguarding medical empathy and cultivating compassion in contemporary medicine
abstract: Empathy and compassion are both fundamental to patient-centred care, enhancing satisfaction, adherence and outcomes while improving clinician well-being. However, certain aspects of medical culture may put these emotional qualities at risk. The preclinical-to-clinical transition exposes students to hierarchical structures, time constraints and performance expectations prioritising technical competence over interpersonal skills. Negative role modelling, rushed consultations and inadequate emotional support normalise emotional detachment. The COVID-19 pandemic intensified burnout and moral injury, while societal desensitisation through social media compounds these effects. Although medical humanities programmes show promise, meaningful change requires addressing both curricula and clinical environments through structured reflection, compassion-focused training and recognising empathy fatigue as an occupational hazard, reaffirming medicine's ethical foundations.

title: Utility of recombinant Schistosoma bovis 22.6 kDa antigen for diagnosis of human urogenital schistosomiasis by ELISA: a cross-sectional study in Yewa North LGA, Ogun State, Nigeria.
abstract: In many endemic regions, accurately diagnosing urogenital schistosomiasis remains challenging, particularly in cases of low-intensity infection and limited laboratory capacity. Exploring antigens that cross-react between related schistosome species provides a promising alternative to conventional diagnostic approaches. Schistosoma bovis-an animal parasite closely related to S. haematobium and sharing the same Bulinus snail hosts in overlapping habitats- is a strong candidate for such studies. This work therefore assessed whether the recombinant S. bovis 22.6 kDa antigen (rSb22.6 kDa) could detect anti-schistosome antibodies in urine samples from individuals living in S. haematobium-endemic communities in Nigeria. Urine samples from 559 individuals (290 adults and 269 children; 235 males and 313 females) from four communities and schools in Yewa North Local Government Area, Ogun State, Nigeria, were collected. Samples were examined for S. haematobium eggs by microscopy, screened for anti-schistosomal antibodies using rSb 22.6 kDa ELISA, and analyzed for haematuria, leukocyturia, and proteinuria using reagent strips. Prevalence by microscopy was 13.9% (78/558), while 54.1% (299/553) of samples were seropositive by ELISA. Among ELISA-positive individuals, 29.8% had haematuria, 47.9% had leukocyturia, and 37.1% had proteinuria. Of 480 microscopy-negative individuals, 221 (46.0%) were ELISA-positive. When microscopy was used as the reference standard, the rSb 22.6 kDa-ELISA showed 46.2% sensitivity and 45.8% specificity. However, ELISA positivity correlated significantly with clinical markers of urogenital pathology (P < 0.05). The rSb 22.6 kDa antigen demonstrated cross-reactivity with antibodies in urine from individuals in S. haematobium-endemic communities. The high seropositivity compared to microscopy prevalence may reflect detection of low-intensity infections, past exposure with persistent antibodies, or ongoing transmission intensity in these communities. While the current performance of the assay does not support its use for individual diagnosis, it shows potential for sero-epidemiological surveillance in endemic areas. Further validation studies incorporating molecular diagnostics and longitudinal follow-up will clarify the significance of antibody positivity in the absence of detectable eggs. Not applicable.

title: Protocol for an agent-based model of recombination in bacteria playing a public goods game.
abstract: Agent-based models are composed of individual agents coded for traits, such as cooperation and cheating, that interact in a virtual world based on defined rules. Here, we describe the use of an agent-based model of homologous recombination in bacteria playing a public goods game. We describe steps for software installation, setting model parameters, running and testing models, and visualization and statistical analysis. This protocol is useful in analyses of horizontal gene transfer, bacterial sociobiology, and game theory. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Lee et al.

title: The effect of cultural socialization on the development of prosocial behavior and academic performance in young adults
abstract: Socialization is a lifelong process of learning that influences an individual’s attitude, behavior, and values. The term “cultural socialization" specifically refers to the learning mechanism by which young adults attain cultural maturity by acquiring awareness of their cultural group values, resulting in the development of a sense of belonging toward that particular cultural group. Family as an agent of socialization plays a crucial role in imparting cultural traits and values to its members, which varies from one family to another due to cultural diversity and social change. The significant influence of peer groups, in addition to family, as a socializing entity adds complexity to this learning system and makes it a potential source for creating distinctions and fostering the development of superiority and inferiority complexes among the members. Young adults who experience socialization from both entities encounter a chaotic state of mind that impacts their behavior and academic performance. Hence, this study seeks to comprehend the significance of cultural socialization in the development of prosocial behavior and academic achievement within diverse cultural contexts, such as educational institutions. The study adopted a quantitative methodology with simple random sampling administered through a questionnaire. The findings show that cultural socialization has a potential influence on academic performance and prosocial behavior. Thus, cultural socialization serves as a catalyst for enhancing prosocial behavior, subsequently leading to better academic performance.

title: Concevoir des esprits sociaux : Comment le design de l'IA et les normes de communication façonnent la perception, l'engagement et le comportement prosocial des humains
abstract: L'importance des agents conversationnels numériques a récemment augmenté, de nombreuses entreprises adoptant des agents pilotés par l'IA pour gérer les demandes d'affaires et faciliter les interactions quotidiennes avec les clients. Étant donné la réticence générale des individus envers l'IA, certaines entreprises choisissent d'anthropomorphiser leurs bots de service client (par exemple, en leur donnant des noms et des avatars). Cependant, l'efficacité de ces pratiques n'est pas claire dans le cas des voicebots (c'est-à-dire, des bots conversationnels basés sur la voix), car ces interventions ne sont pas axées sur la voix. Nous nous concentrons sur la voix, en tant que caractéristique clé des voicebots, et proposons une approche d'anthropomorphisme axée sur la voix. À travers une série de cinq expériences, nous démontrons le rôle de l'attribution d'un accent au voicebot sur les perceptions anthropomorphiques et l'engagement ultérieur des utilisateurs. Plus précisément, nous montrons que les utilisateurs ont une préférence plus marquée pour interagir avec des voicebots et adoptent des attitudes plus positives envers eux lorsque ces voicebots sont équipés d'accents étrangers. Nous mettons en lumière le rôle sous-jacent des perceptions anthropomorphiques en tant que mécanisme psychologique, suggérant que les accents étrangers servent de cue anthropomorphique crucial, influençant l'attitude des utilisateurs et entraînant une préférence pour les voicebots par rapport aux agents en direct. Ces résultats fournissent des éclairages pour les entreprises cherchant à améliorer l'engagement client grâce à leur voicebot, ainsi que pour les entreprises impliquées dans le développement des technologies voicebot

title: The value of a family dinner from the perspective of subjective well-being
abstract: Based on data from the China Family Panel Studies ( CFPS ) 2014 and 2018 surveys, this paper investigates the association between family dinners and subjective well-being ( SWB ), analyzing it through the dual lenses of material and spiritual needs. The findings reveal that sharing meals with family members significantly enhances SWB —and that this positive effect has strengthened over time. Moreover, the magnitude of this effect exhibits notable heterogeneity across urban versus rural residence and across income groups. Employing the life satisfaction approach ( LSA ), the study further monetizes the value of family dinners. On average, residents are willing to pay CNY 11,585 annually for one additional family dinner per week—a willingness-to-pay figure that has also increased over time, again reflecting pronounced urban–rural and income-based disparities. Additional analysis uncovers a threshold effect in the relationship between family dinner frequency and SWB improvement, with the threshold varying by survey year, gender, marital status, and residential location (urban vs. rural).

title: Machine learning in placental research: a review and guide for future studies.
abstract: Machine learning approaches are increasingly applied across biomedical research to analyze complex, high-dimensional datasets and identify patterns that may inform disease diagnosis and biological discovery. In reproductive and placental research, these methods are used to investigate fetal development, pregnancy complications, and early-life health outcomes using molecular and clinical data. Machine learning approaches have widely been applied to placental and obstetric imaging, such as ultrasound, although these applications have been extensively reviewed elsewhere. Despite growing interest, many placental machine learning studies face recurring methodological challenges that limit interpretability and translational relevance. In this review, we summarize common machine learning approaches and concepts relevant to applying machine learning to placental biology. We then examine emerging applications of machine learning in placental research across genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics. We propose best practices for designing robust and reproducible machine learning studies in placental research and highlight future directions, emphasizing prospective prediction and data sharing to support clinically meaningful translation.

title: Building Block-Based Molecular Networking Enables Targeted Isolation of PTP1B-Inhibitory Triterpene-Flavanol Conjugates from the Stems of Tripterygium regelii.
abstract: Celastrol, a quinone methide triterpenoid present in plants of the genus Tripterygium, is a potent leptin sensitizer and a promising scaffold for anti-obesity drug development. Metabolite profiling of the stems of Tripterygium regelii using UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS, combined with building block-based molecular networking (BBMN) analysis, led to the isolation of ten previously undescribed triterpene-flavanol conjugates (1-10), including celastrol derivatives, as well as the annotation of 34 additional congeners sharing a similar core scaffold. The structures of compounds 1-10 were elucidated through comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, chemical derivatization, and quantum chemical calculations. All isolates exhibited configurationally stable sp3-sp2 axial chirality at ambient temperature, and both P- and M-configured atropisomers were identified. In vitro evaluation of protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B) inhibition revealed that compound 10 exhibited potent activity, with an IC50 value of 0.6 ± 0.1 μM, acting as a mixed-type inhibitor. These triterpene-flavanol conjugates represent a new structural class with potential as lead compounds for the development of anti-obesity agents.

title: Jestvirus, a Novel Genus in the Family Autotranscriptaviridae Infecting Aeromonas.
abstract: Aeromonas species are ubiquitous, aquatic, opportunistic pathogens; however, their viral predators remain underexplored. Here, we isolated and characterized Aeromonas phage vB_AsaP_JS1, a dsDNA phage with a short non-contractile tail that infects Aeromonas salmonicida. Comparative analyses indicate that vB_AsaP_JS1 diverges from representative T7-like phages, with gene content similarity below 50% and a maximum amino acid identity of 70% or less. It forms a supported monophyletic clade in both phylogenomic and protein-based trees. Gene-sharing network analysis further shows that vB_AsaP_JS1 and its closest relatives form a distinct, isolated cluster, clearly separated from all currently recognized genera within the family Autotranscriptaviridae and related lineages of Caudoviricetes. Collectively, these features satisfy ICTV criteria for genus demarcation and support the establishment of a novel phage genus, tentatively designated Jestvirus. Functional annotation highlights a compact transcriptional module containing a single-subunit T7-like RNA polymerase and a streamlined replication packaging operon. Several putative host-interaction-related genes, including a deoxycytidine kinase homolog, a PelC-like protein, and a putative glycosidase, are encoded in the genome; their possible roles in nucleotide scavenging or host interaction during infection represent hypotheses that require experimental validation. Metagenomic read mapping reveals sequence-level signals related to vB_AsaP_JS1 in wastewater datasets from multiple geographic regions, suggesting a potentially wider environmental distribution for this phage lineage than previously recognized, though confirmation of phage identity and prevalence will require further investigation. Together, our results expand the known genomic diversity of T7-like phages and provide taxonomic, functional, and ecological evidence for a new phage lineage within Caudoviricetes.

title: Loss of protein function resulting in severe phenotypes of X-linked myotubular myopathy caused by novel synonymous and splice-site variants in the MTM1 gene.
abstract: X-linked myotubular myopathy (XLMTM) is a severe, often neonatally lethal congenital neuromuscular disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the MTM1 gene. Affected neonates typically present with profound hypotonia, generalized muscle weakness, and respiratory insufficiency requiring immediate ventilatory support at birth. Splice-site variants in MTM1 account for approximately 20% of molecularly confirmed cases of XLMTM. Two male neonates with molecularly confirmed severe XLMTM, born at distinct gestational ages, were enrolled. Next-generation sequencing followed by validation with Sanger sequencing identified a de novo synonymous variant (c.183A > G) in MTM1 in Patient 1 and a canonical splice-site variant (c.444+1G > A) in Patient 2. The functional impact of these variants was assessed via longitudinal clinical assessments, skeletal muscle biopsy with histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses, and minigene splicing assays. Minigene assays confirmed pathogenic exon skipping for both variants, with the c.183A > G variant causing complete skipping of exon 4 in Patient 1 and the c.444+1G > A variant causing complete skipping of exon 6 in Patient 2. Both events resulted in frameshifts and the subsequent loss of myotubularin protein expression. Despite sharing severe, life-threatening clinical and histopathological features, including neonatal-onset respiratory failure, centrally located myonuclei, reduced myofiber diameter, and rapid disease progression, the two patients displayed markedly divergent respiratory trajectories. These findings indicate that the novel synonymous variant c.183A > G and the splice-site variant c.444+1G > A in MTM1 can cause comparable lethal phenotypes via pathogenic mechanisms mediated by exon skipping.

title: [Current Systems and Challenges in Acute Ischemic Stroke].
abstract: The devices and techniques used in mechanical thrombectomy have reached a high level of maturity. Over the next decade, the focus will shift from an era of developing treatments and technologies, to one of delivering treatments in a sustainable manner. Key challenges include workforce development, the establishment of healthcare systems to reduce regional disparities in access to care, reimbursement reform and healthcare economics, and physician work-style reform through task shifting and task sharing to allied healthcare professionals. As these issues are closely interconnected, comprehensive policy and system reforms that address them in an integrated manner are urgently required.

title: Neurology and headache medicine in Malawi: territory, education, and the path to strengthening primary care in sub-Saharan Africa.
abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) bears a disproportionate burden of neurological and pain-related diseases while facing a severe shortage of trained specialists. In this context, expanding neurology and, particularly, headache medicine, through education and integration within primary care represents both a necessity and an opportunity. This Perspective proposes a context-sensitive framework in which three interconnected domains-territory, culture, and capacity-shape the accessibility, acceptability, and sustainability of neurological care. Drawing on the experience of the International Headache Society (IHS)-DREAM healthcare network partnership in Malawi, we examine how locally adapted education, task-shifting and task-sharing can contribute to capacity building while highlighting the limitations of approaches that focus on training alone. We argue that closing the neurological treatment gap requires a shift from specialist-centred to system-centred neurology, integrating workforce development with primary care, culturally grounded community engagement, appropriate supervision and referral pathways, supportive national health policies, and equitable access to essential medicines. Task shifting and task sharing between physicians and non-physician clinicians may constitute a sustainable component of this model when appropriately regulated, supervised, remunerated, and integrated with specialist support and referral pathways. Rather than proposing a model for direct transfer across SSA, this Perspective advocates locally led, context-dependent implementation strategies capable of adapting to diverse health systems. Such an approach reframes global neurological capacity building from the episodic transfer of expertise towards the development of resilient and sustainable systems of care.

title: Transcription Factor TabZIP12 Orchestrates the ABA Signaling Pathway to Regulate Drought Tolerance in Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.).
abstract: Drought-induced osmotic stress severely compromises crop yield productivity and threatens global food security. This study reports TabZIP12, a wheat bZIP transcription factor, in regulating osmotic stress tolerance. Under drought and abscisic acid (ABA) treatment, TabZIP12 expression was significantly upregulated with a dose- and time-dependent manner. Y-2H, BiFC, Co-IP, and In vitro pull-down assays confirmed a physical interaction between TabZIP12 and the kinase TaSnRK2.6. This kinase further interacted with the phosphatase TaPP2C50, which in turn interacted with the ABA receptor TaPYL1. These interactions suggest the TabZIP12-involved constitution of a synergistic signaling module (TaPYL1-TaPP2C50-TaSnRK2.6-TabZIP12). Transgene analyses revealed the essential functions of the signaling module members. Of which, TaPYL1, TaSnRK2.6, and TabZIP12 positively while TaPP2C50 negatively regulated drought tolerance, due to their roles in modulating key physiological processes associated with stomatal movement, osmolyte biosynthesis, root morphology, ABA biosynthesis, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging. TabZIP12 possessed an ability in binding with the promoters of critical stress-responsive genes, namely SLAC1 gene TaSLAC1-4, P5CS gene TaP5CS1, PIN-FORMed gene TaPIN3, NCED gene TaNCED3, and APX gene TaAPX6 and activated their activation. Transgenic validation confirmed these genes in positively modulating drought adaptation. Notably, in a wheat variety panel sharing contrasting drought response, the transcripts of TabZIP12 and its target genes correlated significantly with plant dry matter and yield under drought conditions. Haplotype analysis identified TabZIP12-Hap1 as a favorable allele associated with enhanced drought tolerance. Our findings elucidate novel mechanisms underlying the bZIP-mediated drought response and provide valuable genetic resources for breeding drought-resistant wheat varieties.

title: Implementation of Programmatic Mailed Fecal Immunochemical Testing for Colorectal Cancer Screening in the Veterans Health Administration.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted the Veterans Health Administration (VA) to implement programmatic mailed fecal immunochemical test (FIT) screening for colorectal cancer. This paper describes VA's programmatic mailed FIT development, implementation and initial outcomes. VA adapted mailed FIT processes from a Centers for Disease Control and Prevention-sponsored Mailed FIT Implementation Guide, performed regional pilots, created a national Mailed FIT Implementation Team (MFIT), and issued formal policy. The MFIT then provided training and disseminated tools to support VA mailed FIT programs. Programmatic mailed FIT has been implemented in 89.5% of eligible facilities. Between December 1, 2022 and September 30, 2025, 643,933 FIT were ordered and 40.2% were returned. Of those, 89.1% were testable and 10.9% were cancelled, primarily due to missing sample collection date (63.2%) or receipt >15 days after collection (31.5%). Of the 230,427 FIT results, 7.4% were abnormal and colonoscopy was completed in 54.4%. Among 5846 VA colonoscopies, adenomas were detected in 68.0%, and adenocarcinoma was found in 2.3%. Linear regression analysis demonstrated a direct correlation between increasing mailed FIT adoption and the proportion of Veterans who are up to date with screening (r=0.65, p=0.003). VA has successfully developed and disseminated strong practices for population-level CRC screening outreach with programmatic mailed FIT. This practice is associated with moderate levels of adherence and significant improvements in the overall proportion of Veterans who are up to date with screening. Further dissemination of mailed FIT programs, process improvement, and sharing of best practices is ongoing.

title: Systematic benchmarking of multi-ancestry fine-mapping under variant heterogeneity and LD mismatch.
abstract: Increasingly diverse, multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWASs) provide unprecedented opportunities to better understand the genetic architecture of complex traits. In particular, differences in linkage disequilibrium (LD) patterns across populations can be leveraged to improve the resolution and reliability of statistical fine-mapping. However, cross-ancestry effect heterogeneity, population-specific variant support, and LD mismatches pose substantial challenges, motivating a systematic evaluation of multi-ancestry fine-mapping methods to provide practical guidance for analyses across diverse populations. We conducted a comprehensive benchmarking of nine methods, spanning joint probabilistic models that explicitly model cross-ancestry LD and effect sharing, and univariate-based integration approaches that aggregate ancestry-specific results. We evaluated fine-mapping accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency using realistic simulations derived from UK Biobank genotype data, with real-data validation in the All of Us Research Program. Our study revealed that joint modeling approaches achieve improved power and resolution for causal variants shared across populations. In comparison, post-hoc integration is more robust in recovering causal variants present in only a subset of populations by accommodating differences in variant availability. Moreover, methods are generally underpowered in the presence of systematic discrepancies between GWAS summary statistics and external LD reference panels. Motivated by these complementary performance profiles, we propose the multi-ancestry fine-mapping decision strategy, which avoids a priori method selection by adaptively selecting approaches based on locus-level evidence of ancestry-specific variants. Together, our benchmarking and decision strategy offer practical guidance for robust multi-ancestry fine-mapping and highlight the importance of joint modeling that effectively accounts for ancestry-specific variant availability and LD mismatch.

title: Long-acting injectables for global health: drug development considerations and applications in malaria and tuberculosis.
abstract: Long-acting injectable (LAI) drug formulations represent a transformative modality in modern therapeutics, delivering medications that maintain therapeutic effects over extended periods. While initially developed to improve patient adherence and acceptability for applications such as hormonal contraception and chronic conditions, including psychiatric disorders, their recent success in HIV treatment and prevention has catalyzed a growing interest in their application to global health priorities. While there are effective oral drug regimens available for tuberculosis (TB) treatment and malaria chemoprevention, their dosing regimens challenge patient adherence. By providing sustained pharmacological activity over extended periods, LAIs decouple therapeutic efficacy from patient adherence and simplify drug dosing regimens, enhancing real-world effectiveness. This position paper synthesizes the emerging consensus on the application of LAIs for global health from a multidisciplinary expert workshop convened by Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV) and the Gates Foundation in Chicago on March 17-19, 2026. Contributions considered compound selection, formulation design, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic requirements, safety and tolerability profiles, toxicology packages for first-in-human studies, regulatory pathways, and the challenges of human dose prediction. Emphasis was placed on the importance of preclinical-to-clinical translation, particularly through the application of pharmacometric tools and model-informed drug development. The workshop highlighted strategic priorities for advancing the LAI field, including coordinated cross-sector approaches, pre-competitive data sharing, and communities of practice to address critical knowledge gaps. These actions aim to realize the potential for expanding LAI technologies to advance global health.

title: From Trainee Dental Nurse to Dental Therapist and Practice Owner: My Journey Through Dentistry.
abstract: Career pathways within dentistry are increasingly diverse, offering opportunities for progression beyond traditional clinical roles. This opinion piece reflects on the author's personal journey from joining the profession as a trainee dental nurse at the age of 16 to qualifying as a dental therapist and ultimately becoming a practice owner. Along the way, a range of professional and personal challenges have been encountered, including adapting to higher education, overcoming self-doubt, balancing clinical practice with motherhood, and navigating the disruption caused by the Covid-19 pandemic. These experiences strengthened the author's resilience, reinforced the value of lifelong learning, and shaped their approach to patient centred care. The establishment of a practice represented the culmination of years of determination, ambition and professional development. In sharing this journey, the author demonstrates the opportunities available within dentistry and encourages other dental care professionals to pursue their aspirations, regardless of the obstacles they may encounter.

title: AmpliconSuite: an end-to-end workflow for analyzing focal amplifications in cancer genomes.
abstract: Here we present AmpliconSuite, a toolkit for focal amplification analysis from cancer whole-genome sequencing that identifies extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), breakage-fusion-bridges and other amplification modes. Its ecContext module categorizes ecDNA structures to understand formation mechanisms. Validation across 175 metaphase fluorescence in situ hybridization-probed genes in 72 models demonstrated accurate predictions. Analysis of 6,506 patient pan-cancer samples revealed ecDNA-mediated oncogene co-amplification preferences. To democratize data sharing, we created AmpliconRepository, a community-contributable platform, enabling investigation of results across >15,000 publicly hosted samples.

title: Advancing circumpolar maternal and child health: insights from the ICARP IV session.
abstract: This proceedings paper synthesises contributions from a dedicated session on circumpolar maternal and child health held during the International Conference on Arctic Research Planning IV. The objective was to highlight the significance of maternal and child health within Arctic research and to identify community‑anchored, culturally grounded approaches to care across regions. The paper draws on presentations and facilitated dialogue involving researchers, Indigenous midwives, birthworkers, and practitioners, who shared findings related to knowledge dissemination, service delivery, health system structures, and nutrition in the field of maternal and child health. Using a qualitative synthesis of session presentations and a subsequent sharing circle, the paper summarises key themes that illustrate how structural conditions, policy environments, cultural safety, and community strengths shape reproductive health and early‑life wellbeing across Arctic settings. The results demonstrate consistent concerns about cultural safety, evacuation for birth, workforce instability, and the effects of food insecurity, alongside examples of innovative community‑led practices and Indigenous‑centred models of care. The discussion highlights the conceptual importance of cross‑regional learning, Indigenous leadership, and relational models of care for strengthening maternal and child health systems in the circumpolar North. Overall, the paper advances understanding of shared challenges and region‑specific strengths and underscores the need for sustained collaboration, increased documentation of Indigenous‑led models, and policies that support culturally grounded, family‑centred care.

title: Impact of Machine Perfusion on Liver Transplantation for Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Ischemic reperfusion injury (IRI) during liver transplantation is associated with recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Machine perfusion (MP) is associated with a decreased risk of IRI complications. Our study evaluated the role of MP in post-transplant oncologic outcomes in patients with HCC. Adults with HCC transplanted between 2015-2025 from the United Network for Organ Sharing database were divided into MP and no-MP groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) was also performed. Post-transplant HCC recurrence (competing risk) and overall survival (OS) were assessed. Subgroup analysis was performed in populations within and beyond the Milan criteria. A total of 19,466 patients were included in this study. MP was used in 1,392 (7.2%). The MP group had shorter waitlist times, older donors, and more frequent DCDs (p=0.001). After PSM, 512 patients were included in each group (336 patients within Milan criteria in each). In the population beyond Milan after PSM (n=352), MP use was associated with a reduced risk of 1-year and 3-year HCC recurrence (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.09, p=0.02; aHR 0.27, p=0.02). MP use was not associated with the 1-year or 3-year OS (aHR 1.34, p=0.64; aHR 1.32, p=0.54). MP may potentially reduce the risk of HCC recurrence in recipients beyond Milan criteria, without significant difference in OS. However, as MP utilization increases, further validation into the role of MP and oncologic outcomes in larger cohort studies are required.

abstract: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies are transforming our understanding of the normal lung cellular repertoire as well the molecular and cellular networks of chronic lung diseases. In this review we focus on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). title: IDEAL-GENOM: integrated downstream analytical toolkit for genomic analysis.
abstract: There has been an exponential increase in the development of technologies that have offered unprecedented opportunities to unravel the genetic underpinnings of complex traits. However, despite the progress and availability of tools, there are still several challenges to overcome, such as the development of a unified framework that facilitates downstream analysis. To address this challenge, we present IDEAL-GENOM (Integrated Downstream Evaluation And anaLysis toolkit for GENOMic data), a Python-based wrapper designed to streamline the analytical workflow commonly implemented in binary (case-control) genome-wide association studies (GWAS). IDEAL-GENOM integrates widely used tools such as PLINK, GCTA, and bcftools along with custom-developed functionalities, enabling reproducible results through parameter sharing. IDEAL-GENOM provides a simplified framework for quality control (QC), GWAS, and downstream analysis that will enable beginners and advanced users to leverage the built-in functionalities to perform GWAS analysis for complex traits with binary outcomes. IDEAL-GENOM is a customizable tool that enables users to efficiently analyze genotyping data with reproducible QC, post-imputation, and GWAS pipelines.

title: Reproducible analytical pipelines for healthcare discrete‑event simulation: An open guide and worked examples.
abstract: Discrete-event simulation (DES) is a popular technique for exploring problems in healthcare. For these models to be reused and have lasting impact, they need to be reproducible, transparent and well structured. Reproducible analytical pipeline (RAP) approaches are structured robust workflows that ensure analyses can be reproduced. They have emerged as best practice, but modellers struggle to implement them due to gaps in accessible guidance, skills, and time. This paper presents an integrated set of resources designed to help modellers bridge this implementation gap: an open-access e-book and four worked example repositories demonstrating complete RAP workflows for DES in both Python and R. The online book provides step-by-step guidance through nine major sections covering introductory material, project set-up, model inputs, model building, output analysis, experimentation, verification and validation, style and documentation, and collaboration and sharing. The case studies demonstrate varying complexity: a classic M/M/s queueing model, and a replication of a stroke care pathway model. The worked examples serve dual purposes: they demonstrate that RAP principles are achievable for healthcare DES models (from canonical queueing systems to real-world clinical pathways), and they provide templates that modelling teams can adopt and adapt within routine decision-support projects.

title: The wisdom of the diverse crowd(funders)
abstract: Crowdfunding platforms aim to democratize entrepreneurial finance by creating ecosystems that elicit the ‘wisdom of crowds’—aggregating the judgments of individual and often amateur funders. However, there is limited evidence on whether crowds can effectively apply their collective wisdom on these platforms. Our study addresses these questions by analyzing a crowdlending platform that connects Western lenders with borrowers in developing countries. We examine whether lenders effectively screen borrowers, identify platform attributes that influence lenders’ screening accuracy, and uncover the underlying mechanisms driving these effects. To achieve this, we exploit interventions by platform administrators that allow us to observe the counterfactual repayment performance of loans that failed to attract sufficient funding. Our results indicate that rowdlenders can effectively screen creditworthy borrowers, but only when financial information about borrowers is made available. Lenders’ screening effectiveness diminishes substantially for prosocial loans, as many funders converge on similar, socially motivated decisions. These findings provide novel evidence on crowdlenders' performance, highlighting key trade-offs for crowdfunding platforms and offering actionable insights for their administrators.

title: DETERMINING FACTORS OF INTENTION TO PAY ZAKAT VIA FINANCIAL TECHNOLOGY (FINTECH)
abstract: This study aims to examine muzakki’s intention to utilize Financial Technology (Fintech) platforms for paying zakat by investigating the behavioral and psychological determinants. The research integrates the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), with a particular emphasis on prosocial motivations and perceived risk factors. This study uniquely expanded the view of perceived risk variables, including psychological, legal, and time risks, by integrating altruism and empathy as prosocial constructs into a single framework. The research employs a quantitative approach, utilizing a structured questionnaire distributed to 150 purposively selected respondents. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the relationships between the variables. The findings reveal that perceived altruism and empathy significantly influence muzakki’s intention to adopt fintech for zakat contributions. In contrast, perceived risk—which encompasses aspects such as privacy, legality, time, psychological burden, and security—does not have a significant effect on the intention to use fintech for zakat. These results suggest that emotional and social motivations are stronger predictors of digital zakat payment adoption than perceived risk. Therefore, zakat institutions and fintech developers are advised to focus on building trust and emphasizing the altruistic and empathetic values of zakat in their platforms, as this effort is expected to strengthen the development of a sharia-compliant digital financial ecosystem and contribute to achieving social goals, such as poverty alleviation and reducing inequality.

title: The Life-sustenance Hypothesis: Understanding Human-Nature Connection by Integrating Rousseau's Philosophy to Contemporary Systems Biological Viewpoints
abstract: This paper develops the life-sustenance hypothesis to explain the multifaceted phenomenon of the human-nature connection. It is based on an interpretation of Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy brought into contemporary times via recent multidisciplinary research and theoretical underpinnings. Rousseau suggested that humans have two innate, instinctive drives he called amour-de-soi and pitié—a self-preservative drive, and its enlargement, an inclination to help other living beings in distress. The life-sustenance hypothesis is rooted in a systems biological framework situating humans as interconnected parts within a nested system of life. Corresponding to Rousseau’s drives, this interconnectedness is suggested to give rise to the dynamics between two life-preserving orientations that guide our manners-of-being in the world: a self-sustaining and a ‘life-sustaining’ orientation shared by all organisms, albeit manifested differently. The experience of nature connectedness, along with altruistic impulses, are proposed to be human manifestations of the life-sustaining orientation. Moreover, in line with Rousseau’s philosophy, it is posited that the modern, individualistic lifestyle has given rise to an imbalance between these orientations leading to problems in prosociality, proenvironmentalism, and overall well-being. One means by which to regain balanced manners-of-being might be to enhance our nature connectedness. Possible physiological indicators for the hypothesis are explored.

title: Perceptions and Experiences of the Foster Family Program Among Alumni and Undergraduate Medical Students at CMC Ludhiana: An Exploratory Mixed-Methods Study.
abstract: Mentorship plays a crucial role in the holistic development of medical students. The Foster Family Program (FFP) at Christian Medical College (CMC), Ludhiana, is a unique mentorship model that provides academic, emotional, social, and spiritual support through a family-like structure involving faculty mentors ("foster parents") and students ("foster siblings"). To describe and explore foster parents' and foster siblings' retrospective perceptions of the FFP, including reported support, engagement, relationship continuity, strengths, challenges, and suggestions for improvement. A mixed-methods study was conducted among MBBS alumni of CMC Ludhiana (batches 1960-2015), including foster parents and foster siblings. Quantitative data were collected via a structured online questionnaire using snowball sampling and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Qualitative data were obtained through open-ended responses and analyzed using thematic analysis. Key domains assessed included academic performance, mental health, interpersonal relationships, and career development. A total of 227 participants were included, comprising 24 (10.6%) foster parents and 203 (89.4%) foster siblings. The mean age of foster parents was 49.6 years, and that of foster siblings was 21.2 years. Most participants reported positive outcomes, with 15 (65.2%) rating the program highly. Interpersonal relationships were strengthened in 20 (87.0%) of the foster parents, while 14 (60.9%) discussed mental health concerns with their fosters. 120 (61.2%) students reported receiving support during stressful periods, and 109 (55.3%) identified their mentor as inspirational. Long-term relationships persisted, with 17 (77.3%) between foster parents and students, while 13 (6.6%) kept in touch with their foster parents only and 91 (46%) with both foster parents and siblings maintaining contact after graduation. Qualitative analysis revealed key strengths, including emotional support, academic and spiritual guidance, a safe space for sharing, and community bonding. Reported challenges included inactivity of some foster families, time constraints, financial burden, mismatched expectations, and interpersonal discomfort. The FFP was associated with perceived improvements in the academic, psychosocial, and emotional well-being of medical students. While overall perceptions were positive, variability in engagement highlights the need for improved mentor-mentee matching and more structured interaction. The model demonstrates potential for replication, although contextual adaptation may be necessary.

title: The Moving Mandala: Exploring the Pro-Social Effects of Musical and Non-Musical Synchrony in Children in a Virtual World.
abstract: Synchronous movement between individuals has been shown to increase pro-sociality, such as closeness and generosity. To date, synchrony research tests these effects using a variety of movement tasks, including musical and non-musical coordination. However, musical versus non-musical synchrony may have separable pro-social effects. To test this, we had 60 children immersed in an augmented reality space called the 'Moving Mandala' where they moved asynchronously with only visual cues, synchronously with only visual cues or synchronously with musical and visual cues. We then tested for differences in pro-social effects using sharing and proxemics tasks. Results showed that while the synchrony version of the mandala led to greater closeness in the proxemics task, the musical synchrony led to more pro-sociality on the sharing task. The implications of these findings are discussed.

title: The effect of psilocybin on empathy and prosocial behavior: a proposed mechanism for enduring antidepressant effects
abstract: Psilocybin is a serotonergic psychedelic shown to have enduring antidepressant effects. Currently, the mechanism for its enduring effects is not well understood. Empathy and prosocial behavior may be important for understanding the therapeutic benefit of psilocybin. In this article we review the effect of psilocybin on empathy and prosocial behavior. Moreover, we propose that psilocybin may induce a positive feedback loop involving empathy and prosocial behavior which helps explain the observed, enduring antidepressant effects.

title: Drivers of cooperation in social dilemmas on higher‐order networks
abstract: Understanding cooperation in social dilemmas requires models that capture the complexity of real-world interactions. While network frameworks have provided valuable insights to model the evolution of cooperation, they are unable to encode group interactions properly. Here, we introduce a general higher-order networks framework for multi-player games on structured populations. Our model considers multi-dimensional strategies, based on the observation that social behaviours are affected by the size of the group interaction. We investigate the dynamical and structural coupling between different orders of interactions, revealing the crucial role of nested multi-level interactions and showing how such features can enhance cooperation beyond the limit of traditional models with uni-dimensional strategies. Our work identifies the key drivers promoting cooperative behaviour commonly observed in real-world group social dilemmas.

title: How do neurorehabilitation patients perceive their fundamental care needs? Findings from a qualitative study.
abstract: The Fundamentals of Care (FoC) framework provides a structured model to support the delivery of person-centered nursing care by integrating physical, psychosocial, and relational dimensions. Although the framework has been widely applied in acute care, little is known about its relevance in long-term neurorehabilitation settings, where patients often face complex, prolonged, and multidimensional care needs. To explore how individuals with neurological disorders perceive their fundamental care needs during inpatient rehabilitation. A qualitative secondary analysis. A rehabilitation hospital in Italy with a total capacity of 109 beds. We recruited individuals aged 18 years and older with a diagnosis of stroke, multiple sclerosis, or Parkinson disease, or who had undergone neurosurgical intervention for oncological conditions. A deductive content analysis was performed, using the FoC framework to guide coding and thematic development. The analysis identified care experiences across the three FoC dimensions. In the physical dimension, patients valued hygiene, toileting, mobility, and comfort not only as technical tasks but also as meaningful acts that contributed to dignity and recovery. The psychosocial dimension emphasized the importance of respectful communication, emotional support, privacy, and being informed, factors that fostered agency and trust. In the relational dimension, patients highlighted empathy, continuity, and presence as central to feeling emotionally safe and supported. Health care assistants emerged as key figures in delivering comfort-focused and relational care. Across all dimensions, fundamental care was perceived as deeply interconnected and resistant to rigid, task-based models. This study underscores the value of the FoC framework in capturing the multidimensional nature of care as experienced by neurorehabilitation patients. The findings reinforce the need for nurses and assistants to provide care that extends beyond physical tasks to include relational presence and person-centered responsiveness.

title: Resolving social dilemmas with minimal reward transfer
abstract: Abstract Social dilemmas present a significant challenge in multi-agent cooperation because individuals are incentivised to behave in ways that undermine socially optimal outcomes. Consequently, self-interested agents often avoid collective behaviour. In response, we formalise social dilemmas and introduce a novel metric, the general self-interest level, to quantify the disparity between individual and group rationality in such scenarios. This metric represents the maximum proportion of their individual rewards that agents can retain while ensuring that a social welfare optimum becomes a dominant strategy. Our approach diverges from traditional concepts of altruism, instead focusing on strategic reward redistribution. By transferring rewards among agents in a manner that aligns individual and group incentives, rational agents will maximise collective welfare while pursuing their own interests. We provide an algorithm to compute efficient transfer structures for an arbitrary number of agents, and introduce novel multi-player social dilemma games to illustrate the effectiveness of our method. This work provides both a descriptive tool for analysing social dilemmas and a prescriptive solution for resolving them via efficient reward transfer contracts. Applications include mechanism design, where we can assess the impact on collaborative behaviour of modifications to models of environments.

title: Clinical, functional, and quality-of-life characteristics of women with comorbid fibromyalgia and irritable bowel syndrome and their associations with FIQR scores.
abstract: Fibromyalgia (FM) and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) frequently co-occur, sharing pathophysiological mechanisms such as central sensitization and gut-brain axis dysregulation. Given that exercise is a first-line non-pharmacological intervention for FM, detailed baseline characterization may inform future exercise-based research. This study aimed to describe the physical, functional, symptomatic, and quality-of-life profile of women with FM+IBS comorbidity in relation to FM severity, assessed continuously and, secondarily, categorically using the Revised Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQR). This cross-sectional observational study, conducted at IRCCS "Saverio de Bellis" (Castellana Grotte, Bari, Italy), enrolled 33 women (mean age 47.7 ± 8.6 years) diagnosed with FM (2016 ACR criteria) and IBS (Rome IV criteria). Participants were stratified into three groups by FIQR score: Remission/Mild (n=7), Moderate (n=13), and High Severity (n=13). FIQR total score was analyzed as a continuous exposure using Spearman correlations with bootstrapped 95% CIs as the primary analysis; the three-group stratification was retained as a secondary, exploratory presentation. Assessments included pain (VAS), tender points, gastrointestinal symptoms (IBS-SSS), kinesiophobia (TSK), sleep quality (PSQI), physical activity (IPAQ), functional fitness tests, and quality of life (SF-36). Perceived pain showed the strongest association with FIQR severity (Spearman's rho=0.57, p<0.001), with values nearly doubling in the High Severity versus Remission/Mild stratum. Physical activity level (IPAQ; exact p=0.021) differed significantly across FIQR strata, with greater inactivity in the Moderate group. Lower-limb functional strength/endurance, handgrip strength, six-minute walk distance, kinesiophobia, and SF-36 Mental Component Summary were all significantly associated with continuous FIQR (all p<0.05); the Sit-to-Stand difference across categorical strata, significant under standard ANOVA (p=0.048), lost significance under Welch's ANOVA (p=0.148) and Kruskal-Wallis testing (p=0.072). Gastrointestinal burden remained elevated across all groups, with no clear association with FIQR severity (rho=0.29, p=0.097). Sleep quality and SF-36 scores were markedly impaired regardless of FIQR class. In this exploratory sample, greater FM severity was primarily associated with increased pain and reduced lower-limb functional capacity, while gastrointestinal burden remained consistently elevated across the severity spectrum. These descriptive, hypothesis-generating findings may help guide the design of future, adequately powered studies addressing pain threshold, functional capacity, and gastrointestinal tolerance in exercise management of FM+IBS.

title: eLife Assessment: Oxytocin restores context-specific hyperaltruistic preference
abstract: This revised paper provides valuable findings that altruistic tendency during moral decision-making is gain/loss context-dependent and oxytocin can restore the absence of altruistic choices in the loss domain.The methods and analyses are solid, yet the study could still benefit from better overall framing and more clarity and precision in the definition of key constructs, as pointed out by reviewers.If these concerns are addressed, this study would be of interest to social scientists and neuroscientists who work on moral decision-making and oxytocin.

title: Is leisure‐time reading related to empathy and social skills in 8‐ to 10‐year‐old children?
abstract: There is growing interest in the effects of reading on empathy and prosocial behaviour but not enough is known about the associations among these variables in children. In a study undertaken at a single time point, we examined children's leisure reading and self-reported prosocial behaviour, and whether the relation between them was mediated by affective or cognitive empathy or by theory of mind. We tested 113 English-speaking children aged 8-10 years from a UK primary school. Analyses showed that reading and prosocial behaviour are related, and that the relation was partly explained by variance shared with empathy, particularly affective rather than cognitive empathy. Future work focusing on causal aspects of these relations should provide further guidance on the practical implications of these results.

title: MOOD AND EMPATHY ON PROSOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AMONG MUSLIM ADOLESCENTS IN PADANG CITY
abstract: This research is motivated by the phenomenon at the Dharmabakti Nusantara Health Vocational School in Padang City; mood and empathy are thought to influence prosocial behaviour. This study aims to analyse: 1) mood, empathy and prosocial behaviour, 2) the relationship between mood and prosocial behaviour, 3) the relationship between empathy and prosocial behaviour, and 4) the relationship between mood and empathy together with prosocial behaviour. The method used in this study is a Quantitative method that aims to determine the relationship and influence between variables. The research sample was taken from the existing population of 80 students. The research instrument used a questionnaire with a Likert scale model. The data were analysed with descriptive statistics, simple regression, and multiple regression; the results of the research data analysis obtained an R-value of 0.558 with a p level = 0.000 (p <0.05). There is a significant relationship between mood and empathy with prosocial behaviour. R2 =0,311 %. This study proves a positive and meaningful relationship between philosophy and heart in prosocial behaviour at SMK Dharmabakti Nusantara Pota Padang.

title: The Relationship between Well-Being, Empathy, Moral Identity, and Spirituality on Prosocial Behavior among Malaysian Youth
abstract: This study explores the influence of well-being, empathy, moral identity, and spirituality on prosocial behavior among Malaysian youth.A quantitative approach was employed with a sample of 411 participants, using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analyses to investigate the relationships between these variables.The results revealed that moral identity was the strongest predictor of prosocial behavior, followed closely by spirituality, empathy, and well-being.These findings highlight the central role of moral identity in shaping prosocial actions, with spirituality and empathy also playing significant roles.Well-being, while slightly less influential, still contributes meaningfully to prosocial behavior by promoting emotional stability and life satisfaction.The study emphasizes the importance of fostering moral development, spiritual growth, and emotional well-being to encourage prosocial behavior in youth.Policymakers, educators, and community leaders are encouraged to implement programs that focus on these key areas to promote a more compassionate and engaged youth population.

title: Severity over source: Understanding transgressors' motive attributions of punishment
abstract: Punishment conveys social information to transgressors, who attribute motives to punishers. Drawing on the motive-attribution framework, we examined whether transgressors' attributions to competitive (i.e. harming transgressors), individualistic (i.e. managing one's own interests) and prosocial (i.e. healing relationships) motives differ depending on whether punishment is administered by victims (second-party punishment) or uninvolved observers (third-party punishment), and how these attributions relate to downstream affective, relational and behavioural outcomes. In an incentivized Stealing Game, participants could steal valuable points and were punished either by the victim or an observer. Subsequently, transgressors reported their motive attributions, affect and willingness to reconcile and completed a measure of prosocial behaviour towards an unrelated other. Contrary to predictions, motive attributions did not systematically differ between second- and third-party punishment, except that third-party punishment was more strongly attributed to reputational concerns (i.e. a subdimension of individualistic motive attribution). Punishment severity emerged as an important predictor, with harsher sanctions linked to stronger competitive and individualistic attributions. Competitive motive attribution, in turn, was associated with higher negative affect and lower positive affect, willingness to reconcile and prosocial behaviour. Overall, transgressors' responses to punishment were less clearly shaped by who punished and more closely linked to punishment severity and motive attribution.

title: The Role of the Effectiveness of Mosque Social Activities and Their Consistency in Repetition Donation Decisions (Case Study of Masjid Raya Al Insan)
abstract: Mosques play a vital role in Islam, serving not only as places of worship but also as centers for various social activities and economic empowerment, including the collection of social funds such as zakat, infaq, and sadaqah (charity). However, data from the 2024 Mosque Information System (SIMAS) of the Ministry of Religious Affairs of the Republic of Indonesia shows that of the total 694,725 mosques and prayer rooms, only 28,138 have a Mosque Welfare Agency (BKM), indicating that the majority of mosque management remains traditional and has not adopted modern management. Masjid Raya Al Insan (MRAI) in Kebayoran Lama, South Jakarta, is known for frequently holding social and humanitarian activities, both routine and incidental, for the congregation and the community living around the mosque. Previous research has examined factors such as transparency, accountability, the attitude of mosque management, and the social and religious influences of donors on trust and donation decisions. However, there is still little research that specifically examines the role of the effectiveness of mosque social activities and their consistency on repeat donation decisions. Using a qualitative case study method through in-depth interviews with administrators and donors, this study evaluates the role of the effectiveness and consistency of MRAI's social programs on repeat donations. The results show that the effectiveness of social activities is assessed by the emotional impact and tangible solutions for the community, not simply by statistical figures. It was found that repeat donation decisions are driven by a strong synergy between theological motivation and trust in the integrity of the administrators. Specifically, the consistency of social programs proved to be a key factor in building donor loyalty, validating the paradigm that "busy mosques" that actively distribute funds actually attract more donations. The study concluded that program consistency creates a sense of security and inner satisfaction for donors. As a recommendation, mosque administrators need to immediately undertake digital transformation in transparent financial reporting and implement Customer Relationship Management (CRM) to maintain donor relationships to ensure the sustainability of funding for community programs.

title: Random Forest for Multi-Output Analysis of University Students' Prosocial Behaviors
abstract: This study examines differential effects that different demographic variables and the subgroup-based community management model in universities on college students' prosocial behavior. Our dataset includes survey responses from 307 students enrolled in universities implementing this management model and 200 students from non-implementing universities. We employed the Random Forest algorithm to training AI model on 90% of the participant sample and reserving the remaining 10% for validation. The model achieved a prediction accuracy of 96.08%, demonstrating strong reliability in assessing the relationship between community-based subgroup management and prosocial behavioral outcomes. Furthermore, Random Forest shows the importance of independent variables.

title: How social norms emerge: the interindividual actor-critic
abstract: Social norms shape a vast range of human behaviors, from everyday interactions to major life choices. Yet, existing theories of norm emergence typically focus either on why certain norms arise (substantive properties) or on how they spread and persist (dynamical properties), often making conflicting assumptions. Here, we propose a unified account in which norms prescribing how one ought to act emerge naturally from the fundamental algorithms that guide learning—whether in social or non-social settings. Our account builds on recent advances in decision-making and emotion research that have highlighted ‘actor-critic’ models as a core mechanism of learning from feedback. We extend this mechanism to social settings by assuming that it is not only we who critique our actions, others critique our actions as well. By simulating this interindividual form of learning, we show that it uniquely produces group behavior that exhibits both substantive and dynamical properties of real-world social norms, including prosociality, ingroup bias, stickiness, S-shaped curves, and local conformity / global diversity. Our framework thus offers a uniquely parsimonious way to bridge the gap between individual learning and group behavior.

title: Product Management Experiences of Patients With a Stoma Receiving Telenursing Services.
abstract: This study explored how individuals with a stoma interpret and manage product-related challenges and examined the contribution of telenursing services to their daily care processes. A qualitative descriptive design. Seven participants were recruited through criterion-based purposive sampling among individuals receiving telenursing support for stoma care from a private healthcare provider. Data were collected through online semi-structured interviews lasting 20-30 min and analysed using conventional content analysis with MAXQDA 24 software. The study was reported according to COREQ guidelines. Ethical approval was obtained from the Bahçeşehir University Scientific Research and Publication Ethics Committee prior to data collection (decision no. 2024/07, dated 1 August 2024). All participants provided written informed consent, and institutional approval was obtained before the study commenced. Five overarching themes were identified: reasons for using telehealth, recommendations received through telenursing, emotional responses following telehealth, perceived effectiveness of counselling and alternative methods sought by patients. Participants reported that telenursing provided practical, timely and personalised guidance that helped them manage issues such as adapter leakage, skin irritation, product selection and wound assessment. Participants reported needing fewer hospital visits and described feelings of safety, satisfaction and relief. While some participants consulted physicians or the internet for additional information, telenursing remained their primary and trusted source of support. Participants described telenursing as supporting their self-care capacity and as a source of practical guidance and reassurance in managing product-related problems. These accounts suggest that integrating telehealth into routine stoma care may strengthen continuity of care, although the present design does not allow its effects on clinical outcomes to be determined. Health professionals should consider expanding digital care competencies and developing structured telenursing protocols to strengthen this form of support. Participants' accounts suggest that structured telenursing support may help individuals with a stoma manage practical, product-related difficulties in daily life. Stoma nurses and telenurses can use these findings to inform product-use education, routine skin assessment, leakage management, structured follow-up contacts, timely escalation to physicians and the development of digital communication protocols. What problem did the study address? Individuals living with a stoma frequently encounter difficulties with product selection, adapter fit, leakage and peristomal skin care, yet little is known about how these difficulties are experienced in everyday life, or how telenursing responds to them from the patients' own perspective. What were the main findings? Participants' accounts centred on practical product problems such as adapter leakage, peristomal irritation and wound care. They described the remote guidance they received as prompt and dependable, said it left them feeling more secure and better able to manage their own care, and reported turning to hospital services less often than they otherwise would have. Other information sources were consulted, but telenursing was consistently placed ahead of them. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The findings are relevant to stoma care nurses and telenurses, and to the healthcare organisations that provide remote follow-up for individuals living with a stoma. The study adhered to the EQUATOR Network guidelines and was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) checklist. Participants contributed to the study by sharing their experiences in individual interviews and by reviewing summaries of their own interviews as part of member checking, which informed the verification of the interpretations reported here. Patients or members of the public were not involved in the design of the study, in the development of the interview guide, or in the preparation of the manuscript.

title: Melioidosis in South Asia: Scientific Advances, Regional Challenges and One Health Perspectives-An Integrated Research Synthesis from the 4th South Asian Melioidosis Congress.
abstract: Melioidosis, caused by We conducted an integrated narrative synthesis of the scientific content presented at the Congress, including plenary lectures, oral and poster presentations, panel discussions, and case-based deliberations. Topics encompassed epidemiology, clinical manifestations, laboratory diagnostics, genomics, treatment strategies, outbreak investigations, antimicrobial resistance, and One Health perspectives across South and Southeast Asia. The Congress highlighted expanding geographic recognition of melioidosis across India and neighbouring countries, with reported cases likely representing only a small fraction of the true disease burden. Clinical discussions emphasized marked heterogeneity in presentation and strong associations with diabetes mellitus, environmental exposure, and the monsoon season. Advances in diagnostics included broader implementation of MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, molecular assays, and rapid diagnostic tests, although significant gaps remain in laboratory capacity, surveillance, and clinical recognition. Genomic investigations demonstrated substantial strain diversity while identifying conserved virulence determinants that may support surveillance and outbreak investigations. Participants also underscored the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration, standardized diagnostic practices, and regional data sharing to improve case detection and patient outcomes. Melioidosis remains an underrecognized but increasingly important public health challenge in South Asia. Strengthening surveillance systems, expanding diagnostic capacity, improving clinician awareness, fostering regional laboratory networks, and adopting coordinated One Health strategies are essential to reduce morbidity and mortality. The Congress also reinforced the need for sustained advocacy toward recognition of melioidosis as a neglected tropical disease.

title: Evaluation of Co-Production in Adolescent Health Research: A Mixed Methods Study From Born in Bradford.
abstract: Co-production is often viewed as best practice for involving the public in research, while measures such as sharing power, reciprocity, and relationship-building are seen as key guiding principles. However, implementing co-production and its underlying principles remains challenging, with limited evaluative work examining how these principles are applied in practice, particularly within large-scale studies and with young people. This study aimed to explore whether Born in Bradford's (BiB) co-production values and principles have been embedded in BiB Age of Wonder (AoW), a longitudinal study following over 20,000 Bradford teenagers through secondary school and into early adulthood. This evaluation used a mixed-methods approach. Participants included parents, young people, teachers, and community members. Quantitative data was collected via an online survey (n = 79). Qualitative data was collected via four focus groups (n = 17). The survey and focus group topic guide were co-designed with young people, with questions designed to assess how well the principles and values of BiB's co-production strategy had been embedded in AoW. Descriptive statistics were used to explore the survey responses. Qualitative data was analysed using framework analysis. Survey and focus group findings indicated that co-production group members mostly agreed or strongly agreed that the nine principles of co-production had been embedded in AoW. However, 'sharing power' and 'community engagement' were found to be areas that could be improved, with participants calling for earlier involvement in research design, clearer feedback loops, and outreach beyond existing groups. We found evidence that the values and principles of co-production have been embedded in AoW co-production. Suggestions for improvement include shaping research agendas through earlier involvement, deeper engagement with schools and communities, and paid peer research posts. Future steps include (1) developing sustainable peer research strategies to deepen co-production, and (2) incorporating perspectives from diverse stakeholders including budget holders, facilitators, researchers and public contributors in future evaluations. Members of the public were involved in the study conceptualisation, methods development and implementation. The survey and focus group topic guide were co-designed with young people from BiB Age of Wonder co-production groups. Co-production group members were also involved as participants in the surveys and focus groups.

title: Comparing harmonization in medicines regulation and health technology assessment in Europe: lessons for the EU HTA regulation.
abstract: The European Union (EU) has long pursued harmonization in medicines regulation and, more recently, in health technology assessment (HTA). The European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the EU HTA Regulation (EU HTAR) represent key milestones in these respective trajectories. This study compares the harmonization trajectories of EU medicines regulation and EU HTA to identify lessons relevant for EU HTAR implementation. We used a multi-method qualitative approach combining a narrative literature review with online focus groups involving eighteen regulatory and policy experts. The review explored the historical development of harmonization in both policy areas. The focus-group analysis examined perspectives on collaboration, harmonization dynamics, and implementation. Both policy areas moved from national arrangements and voluntary cooperation toward more formal EU-level structures. Medicines regulation developed earlier and resulted in more centralized procedures and binding EU-wide authorization decisions. EU HTA retains greater national responsibility for value judgments, pricing, and reimbursement. The two areas also differ in the scope and standardization of assessments. In both trajectories, harmonization was shaped by trust, willingness to collaborate, capacity differences, and legal and procedural contexts. Participants emphasized the importance of stepwise implementation, work sharing, and sustained dialogue, while anticipating variation in national JCA uptake and impact. Experience from EU medicines regulation highlights the importance of building trust and adapting collaboration to differences in national maturity and priorities. Harmonization should develop gradually through learning and refinement across diverse legal and procedural contexts. These lessons may support EU HTAR implementation and further development.
